name: Blaxel

modes.label: Sandbox (active time, RAM-only pricing, CPU bundled)
modes.note: $0.0000115 per GB of allocated RAM per active second ($0.0414/GB-h); CPU derived from memory (8 GB = 4 cores, 16 GB = 6 cores) and not charged. Billed only while a connection is active; auto-standby ~15 s after last connection (then snapshot storage only). CPU utilisation does not reduce the bill. Writable FS is tmpfs (~50% of RAM), no separate disk.
modes.perf_source: StarSling hpc-sandbox-benchmarks, run 36498291449 (2026-09-29), Node.js V8 Web Tooling p50 at a 4 vCPU / 8 GB target

modes.label: Batch Jobs (non-interactive tasks, max 24 h)
modes.note: $0.000006/GB RAM-s 'billed by the memory it uses' (possibly used rather than allocated RAM; alloc assumed = upper bound). Only valid for batch/job workloads: no standby, no interactive sessions, 24 h max per task, ~30 s boot. RAM-per-core of 2 GB assumed from sandbox/app sizing (not documented for jobs). Basis verified 2026-09-28: Pricing page: sandboxes "billed by its allocated memory"; batch jobs "Active compute across every task in a job, billed by the memory it uses." (https://blaxel.ai/pricing). Contrast suggests used RAM but not defined; kept alloc.

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go Tier 0 (free)
plans.note: Free credits only; forced TTL <= 7 days; cannot request quota increases. 4 GB cap from earlier research, not re-verified.

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go Tier 1
plans.note: Unlocked by >= $20 real top-ups in trailing 30 days; top-up goes to wallet as usage credit. Forced TTL <= 30 days. Standby sandboxes count toward the 50 limit.

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go Tier 2
plans.note: Unlocked by >= $50 top-ups / 30 days; unlimited standby persistence.

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go Tier 9
plans.note: Contact sales; tiers 3-8 thresholds/limits not public.

plans.name: Custom
plans.note: Quote; volume pricing, private networking, bring-your-own-metal, custom SLA/hardware.

features.ip_note: Shared Blaxel public IPs by default; dedicated egress IPs (private preview, on request) and outbound proxy with header/body injection; no residential proxies documented.

perf_source: Sandbox and Batch Jobs are different runtimes: perf is on the sandbox mode only.

knobs.label: Share of session with an open connection
knobs.why: Blaxel bills allocated RAM only while the sandbox is active, i.e. has an open connection or keepAlive process (not CPU use); ~15 s after the last connection closes it drops to standby and pays snapshot storage only. Clients that disconnect between agent steps pay a fraction of wall-clock; an idle WebSocket/TCP connection keeps billing for up to 15 min and keepAlive (timeout 0) forever, so 1 (default) = whole session billed.

caveats: Billing is on allocated RAM x ACTIVE time, where active = has an open connection (not CPU utilisation). Engine running hours = wall-clock session hours; real bills can be much lower if clients disconnect between steps (auto-standby ~15 s after last connection) or higher if idle WS/TCP connections (up to 15 min) or keepAlive processes hold the sandbox active.
Standby snapshot storage ($0.20/GB-month) appears to be billed on ~allocated memory size (vendor example: 2 GB sandbox in standby 1 month = $0.40); persistent fleets pay this for every standby hour.
Archive (private preview) stops snapshot billing; archive storage price not published.

Tier 'fee' is a rolling 30-day top-up volume deposited as wallet credit (not a fee); tier downgrades if top-ups lapse, even with balance. Promo credits do not count. Whether wallet credit expires is not documented.
Sandbox-count quota includes standby sandboxes; an unpublished per-tier account memory quota also exists. Tiers 3-8 not public.
Tier 0/1 force max TTL 7/30 days; unlimited persistence needs Tier 2+.
Support add-ons carry a % of usage surcharge (3% / 10%) the card cannot model.
Minimum billed seconds per resume not documented.
Writable FS is tmpfs ~50% of RAM; extra disk = Volume at $0.12/GB-month on PROVISIONED size (disk_gib_month here = volume price). Images $0.045/GB-month not modelled.
Sizes above 16 GB: core count undocumented (third-party cites XL 32 GB at $1.3248/h); up to 256 GB on Custom only.
Batch Jobs mode is only valid for non-interactive tasks <= 24 h; MCP hosting ($0.0252/GB-h) omitted as a mode.
No public inbound IPv4; dedicated egress IPs/gateway/proxy free during beta. Wildcard custom domains $20/domain-month.
'Up to $200' free credits: exact amount not specified.
Blaxel acquired by Baseten (2026-09-10); product/pricing stated unchanged.
unverified: batch jobs may bill active (used) RAM, per "billed by the memory it uses" (https://blaxel.ai/pricing); card keeps alloc as the upper bound.

Features check 2026-09-28: nested_virt null -> false. Blaxel: "Each sandbox runs in a dedicated Firecracker microVM with its own kernel" (blaxel.ai/blog/soc-2-compliant-sandbox-providers); Firecracker test_nv.py asserts guests have no nested virtualization (/dev/kvm absent). Desktop = official blaxel/xfce-vnc hub image; Docker = official blaxel/docker-in-sandbox image.

Standby delay conflict: pricing FAQ says sandboxes scale to zero after ~5 s of inactivity, but the lifecycle docs and blog still say ~15 s after the last connection. Card keeps 15 s (conservative); if 5 s is right, disconnected sessions bill ~10 s less each.

fleet.verification: Real wallet top-ups over trailing 30 days; promotional credits and existing balance do not qualify.
fleet.tiers: Tier 0 10; Tier 1 50 after $20/30 days; Tier 2 200 after $50/30 days; Tier 9 100,000+ by contact. Other thresholds are in console.
fleet.notes: Quota includes standby as well as active sandboxes. Tier continuously adjusts with rolling top-ups and can decrease; free tier cannot request increases, paid tiers can request review in console. Tier 0/1 TTL caps 7/30 days. 300/1,000 eligibility thresholds and human approval turnaround are not public.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: When transitioning to standby mode, Blaxel automatically creates a snapshot of the entire state (including the complete file system in memory, preserving both files and running processes) and transitions the sandbox to standby mode within approximately 15 seconds.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: no active connection for ~15 s (idle WS/TCP connections count as inactive after 15 min). Memory + running processes + FS included; resume <25 ms on reconnect. Snapshot storage billed. Separate Archive (private preview) drops memory.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A snapshot captures the state of a sandbox at a point in time: its filesystem, its running processes, and its memory. Use snapshots to checkpoint a sandbox before a risky change, to roll it back later, or as the basis for forking a new sandbox.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Private preview (Carbon / Mark 3.1). Memory included; in-place rollback or fork into new sandboxes; snapshots outlive the source sandbox.

harness_api.quote: Connect to the Claude Code sandbox terminal:
harness_api.note: Claude Code / Codex hub images exist (agent_harnesses), but they are driven interactively via `bl connect sandbox` or by an external harness (Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, DeepSeek Harness plugin) using the sandbox as a tool backend via MCP. No first-party prompt/stream/resume API for a harness in the API reference (Agents Hosting = deploy your own agent code as an endpoint).

egress_allowlist.quote: To enforce filtering even for tools that bypass those variables, add a `firewall` config with `rulesets: ["proxy"]`. This locks down the sandbox's egress at the network level so that all outbound traffic must flow through the proxy.
egress_allowlist.note: allowedDomains / forbiddenDomains with wildcards, updatable on a running sandbox. Without firewall ruleset it only relies on HTTP(S)_PROXY env vars (bypassable). Enforcement set only at creation and only on Mark 3.0 (not Carbon). Private ranges/169.254.169.254 always bypass the proxy. No IP/CIDR egress rules documented.

egress_http_rules.quote: You can also scope a rule to specific HTTP methods and URL paths by adding method prefixes and a path suffix:
egress_http_rules.note: Pattern [!]METHOD:...:domain[/path]; path prefix canonicalized. No header-based rules; the proxy also injects headers/body fields.

ingress_rules.quote: This preview URL can be either **public** (does not require you to be authenticated to access it) or **private** (see below).
ingress_rules.note: Per-port preview URLs chosen by you; private ones need a bl_preview_token query param or X-Blaxel-Preview-Token header (expiring tokens). No public IPv4 / raw TCP; no inbound IP allowlist documented.

guest_firewall.quote: By default, sandboxes run on a minimal kernel without iptables support. You can enable iptables by passing `extraArgs` at creation time.
guest_firewall.note: Firecracker microVM with root; iptables only when created with extraArgs {iptables: enabled} (used by Tailscale tutorial).

secret_proxy.quote: Secrets are resolved server-side by the proxy — the sandbox runtime never sees raw secret values
secret_proxy.note: Public preview. MITM HTTPS proxy; per-destination routing rules inject {{SECRET:name}} into headers/body for any host; write-only secrets. HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and gRPC (header injection only on streams); no database/SSH/raw TCP credential injection documented.

volume_attach.quote: At this time, you can only attach one volume to a sandbox. A volume can also only be attached to one sandbox at a time.
volume_attach.note: Block volumes, attach only at sandbox creation, cannot detach; $0.12/GB-month provisioned.

volume_shared.quote: Drives support concurrent read-write access (RWX) from multiple sandboxes simultaneously, with built-in replication for durability.
volume_shared.note: Agent Drive: private preview, us-was-1 only; FUSE distributed FS, hot-mount on running sandboxes, read-write or read-only mounts, label-based ACLs, S3-compatible endpoint. Block Volumes themselves are single-attach.
